Learn how to build a real website without code in three steps using AI chat, with a working example prompt.", "targetKeyword": "how to build a website without code", "category": "Guides", "bodyHtml": "

For most of the last decade, "building a website without code" meant one thing: dragging boxes around in a template builder. That approach works, but it comes with a ceiling. This guide covers why the old way is limited, how the new AI-chat approach is different, and the exact steps to build and publish a real site today.

Why "without code" used to mean drag-and-drop

Classic website builders let you place pre-made blocks on a page and adjust colors, fonts, and spacing through a visual editor. That is genuinely easier than hand-writing HTML and CSS, and it is why the category took off. But the tradeoffs are real:

  • Generic look. Everyone is assembling the same block library, so sites built this way tend to look like each other.
  • Limited customization. The moment you want something the block library was not designed for, you hit a wall — you are editing a template, not building a site.
  • No real codebase. What the builder outputs is proprietary markup tied to that platform, not a project you actually own or can extend later.

The new approach: describe it, get real code

The alternative that has emerged is chat-based generation: you describe the site you want in plain English, and instead of manipulating a fixed set of blocks, an AI writes an actual codebase for you. There is no editor to fight with because there is no editor step at all — you are directing the build in conversation.

On Kodely, this is not a mockup or a page of raw HTML. Every project is a real Vite + React 19 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS v4 application, built from a foundation codebase with hand-built UI primitives (Button, Card, Section, Nav) as the starting point. The output is component files you could open in an editor and recognize as a normal modern web app, because it is one.

How to build a website on Kodely: 3 steps

1. Describe your site

Open a new project and describe what you want in the chat interface. Be as specific as you would be briefing a developer — more on what to include below.

2. Watch the live preview

As Kodely generates the components, the live preview renders the actual compiled app, not a static image of it. You are looking at the real site.

3. Publish

When it looks right, click Publish. Your site goes live immediately on a free URL at <yourname>.kodely.site — included, with no separate hosting step or cost to set up.

A real example prompt

Vague prompts produce vague sites. Here is the level of detail that gets a usable first result:

Example prompt: "Build a landing page for a mobile app called Driftline that helps freelancers track billable hours. Include a hero section with the app name, a one-line pitch, and a call-to-action button labeled Get Early Access. Below that, three feature cards: automatic time tracking, client invoicing, and weekly summary reports. Use a dark background with a teal accent color, and end with a simple footer with a contact email."

That single prompt gives Kodely a page structure, specific copy points, and a visual direction — enough to generate something close to usable on the first pass.

If the first result is not quite right

You do not start over. Describe the change in chat the same way you would ask a developer for a revision: "make the hero text bigger," "change the accent color to orange," "add a pricing section below the features." Kodely edits the real components behind the scenes rather than regenerating the whole project.

Every successful generation is saved as a checkpoint, so if a change goes in a direction you do not like, rolling back to the previous version is free.

Common mistakes when writing your first prompt

  • Being too vague. "Build me a website for my business" leaves every decision to guesswork. Name the sections you want, the tone, and any specific copy or colors that matter to you.
  • Asking for too much at once. A first prompt that tries to spec an entire multi-page site with a dozen features is harder to get right in one pass than a focused homepage you then build on. Start with the core page, check the preview, then add sections one instruction at a time.

Going live

Publishing is a single click and it is free — your site is reachable at its .kodely.site address right away. Every publish is automatically scanned for accidentally leaked secrets or API keys before it goes live, so you are not shipping a stray key by mistake. There are no custom domains yet, so your live URL will be on the kodely.site subdomain.

If you want to keep working on the site later, you can open the project again, view and copy the actual generated source files from the code view, and keep describing changes in chat. There is no project export or zip download yet — changes happen in-app.

What it costs

Kodely runs on credits tied to real AI generation cost. You get 750 credits free on signup, no credit card required. If a generation fails to compile, Kodely attempts one automatic repair — and you are never charged for a build that fails.

FAQ

Do I need to know how to code?

No. You describe what you want in plain English and Kodely writes the code. You can view the generated source in-app if you are curious, but you never have to touch it.

Is the output a real website or a template?

It is a real Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind codebase generated for your specific description, not a shared template with your text dropped in.

Can I use my own domain?

Not yet — today every published site lives at a free .kodely.site subdomain.

Can I add a database, login, or payments?

Not yet. Kodely currently generates the front-end application — the pages, layout, and components — not backend features like auth or payments.

What if I mess something up?

Every successful generation is a checkpoint. Roll back to any previous version for free.
